title: Worker-critic iteration record
description: One record per worker-critic round, emitted by the loop and by the evaluation runner. This is the canonical superset: the live loop populates the core fields, the evaluation runner additionally populates case_id, case_set_id and assertion results. Recovery rate (alpha) is nullable and computed downstream — never self-reported by the loop being measured.

artefact_id.description: e.g. PROJ-412 or a document slug

origin.description: Frozen-set runs are what separate model drift from context drift. Keep them in the same store as production runs or you cannot compare them.

assertions.description: Populated on evaluation runs only. One entry per assertion in the case.

verdict.description: The round's verdict, in the loop's token vocabulary — a critic's, or the finalizer's machine rejection, as verdict_source says. Maps one-for-one onto the review file: '### VERDICT: APPROVED' -> APPROVED, '### VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED' -> CHANGES_REQUESTED. The other token sets belong to other surfaces and never appear here: READY / NOT_READY is the Spec Quality field of the readiness block, and GATE_PASS / GATE_FAIL is the author's self-check. NEEDS_WORK is not a verdict anywhere. Widen this enum and the aggregation silently drops the non-approving rounds, which are the whole signal for escalation rate and recovery rate.

verdict_source.description: Who issued this round's verdict. `critic`: a critic seat's verdict token, mapped as `verdict` describes; in a code round it reviewed a candidate the finalizer had passed, and `finalizer` records that run. `finalizer`: test-guard.mjs finalize exited 1 on the round — a deterministic machine rejection (nothing to review, the guard's hooks tampered with, or the repository's own checks on the candidate), never a critic's; a protected change alone is undone, not rejected. No critic was dispatched, so `critic` is absent, `signal_source` is `machine`, `verdict` is `CHANGES_REQUESTED` and `quality` is 0. The round still spends one of the code loop's rounds. A record without this field predates the finalizer and carries a critic's verdict.

finalizer.description: The finalizer's run on the round (test-guard.mjs finalize): the engineer's HEAD it took, the one candidate commit and tree it built from that HEAD and checked — every approved test as in the approved test commit, every refused new path taken out — and what it found. Detail beyond these counts stays in the temporary run directory and is removed with it.

candidate_sha.description: The candidate commit, or the engineer's HEAD where the round was refused before one was built.

raw_sha.description: The engineer's HEAD as handed in.

restored.description: Approved entries the engineer's HEAD edited, deleted, replaced or re-moded, restored by the finalizer. Never a reason on its own to fail the round.

removed.description: New paths the engineer's HEAD added in protected locations — a test it wrote included — taken out by the finalizer.

failed_checks.description: The checks.env keys whose command failed in the finalizer's checkout.

alpha.description: Null at iteration 0. Computed downstream, never self-reported.

context_fingerprint.description: Hash of constitution + rule pack + skills in force for this run. Without it you can see drift and cannot explain it.

agent.description: agent_id as it appears in the agent registry. An unregistered agent_id here is a governance failure, and the aggregation job should reject the record.
